lessons.title: Emergency Pharmacology & Medication Safety
lessons.summary: ความผิดพลาด EMS มักเกิดจาก concentration, decimal, weight, route หรือ unit ไม่ใช่การจำชื่อยาไม่ได้. บทนี้เน้นระบบป้องกัน error.

sections.title: 1) Dose language
paragraphs: แยก mg, mg/kg, mcg/kg/min, mL และ concentration ให้ชัด. คำนวณ dose ก่อน แล้วค่อยแปลงเป็น volume.

sections.title: 2) Weight-based dosing
paragraphs: ใช้ actual measured weight เมื่อเป็นไปได้. Estimated weight โดยเฉพาะ neonate/เด็กเล็กเป็น safety risk และต้อง double-check.

sections.title: 3) Concentration traps
paragraphs: Epinephrine เป็น classic high-risk example: concentration ต่างกันตาม indication/route. แอปต้องโชว์ mg และ mL พร้อม concentration ทุกครั้ง.

sections.title: 4) Independent double-check
paragraphs: High-alert medication ควร verbalize: patient weight, indication, dose, concentration, volume, route, max dose และ time given.

sections.title: 5) Infusions
paragraphs: ก่อนเริ่ม infusion ให้ยืนยัน drug amount, diluent volume, final concentration, dose unit, pump rate and compatible line.

key_points: Use leading zero; avoid trailing zero
quick_review: 0.1 mg ≠ 0.1 mL unless concentration says so

sources.label: AHA/AAP drug tables and local medication protocols

quiz.q: หลักที่ปลอดภัยที่สุดก่อนแปลงยาเป็น mL?
options: คำนวณ dose ที่ต้องการเป็น mg/mcg ก่อน
ใช้ mL อย่างเดียว
ไม่ต้องดู concentration
quiz.explain: Dose and concentration must be separated before calculating volume.

lessons.title: Emergency Analgesia & Sedation Pharmacology
lessons.summary: เลือกยาโดยจับคู่ indication + hemodynamics + airway risk + duration ไม่ใช่จำ dose อย่างเดียว.

sections.title: 1) Analgesics
paragraphs: Opioids provide potent analgesia but can cause respiratory depression/hypotension; ketamine provides analgesia/dissociation with different hemodynamic profile; acetaminophen/NSAIDs have roles and contraindications.

sections.title: 2) Sedatives
paragraphs: Benzodiazepines, propofol, ketamine and other agents differ in onset, duration, respiratory and cardiovascular effects.

sections.title: 3) Safety bundle
paragraphs: Indication, weight, concentration, dose, route, allergy, monitoring, rescue equipment and reassessment must be explicit.

sections.title: 4) Special populations
paragraphs: Elderly, shock, pregnancy, renal/hepatic failure and polypharmacy require more cautious titration.

lessons.title: Vasopressor & Inotrope Pharmacology
lessons.summary: เข้าใจ receptor effect และ disease phenotype ก่อนเลือกยา.

sections.title: 1) Norepinephrine
paragraphs: Predominantly alpha with some beta effect; widely used for vasodilatory septic shock.

sections.title: 2) Epinephrine
paragraphs: Strong alpha/beta effects; central in cardiac arrest/anaphylaxis and used in selected shock states, but can increase lactate and tachyarrhythmia.

sections.title: 3) Dobutamine
paragraphs: Inotropic beta effect can improve cardiac output in selected pump failure but may lower SVR/BP.

sections.title: 4) Administration safety
paragraphs: Concentration, infusion pump, dedicated line/site monitoring and extravasation plan are essential; peripheral initiation policies vary.

lessons.title: Emergency Antiarrhythmics: Mechanism, Rhythm and Toxicity
lessons.summary: antiarrhythmics can be proarrhythmic—match drug to rhythm and hemodynamic context.

sections.title: 1) Amiodarone
paragraphs: Broad-channel effects; used in selected ventricular arrhythmias and arrest algorithms. Hypotension/bradycardia and long-term toxicities matter.

sections.title: 2) Lidocaine
paragraphs: Sodium-channel blocker useful as an alternative for ventricular arrhythmias in resuscitation pathways; neurologic toxicity can occur with high exposure.

sections.title: 3) Adenosine
paragraphs: Very short AV nodal blockade; useful for selected regular SVT and diagnostic use in regular monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia under algorithm. It does not terminate AF/flutter and can be dangerous in some pre-excited rhythms.

sections.title: 4) Magnesium
paragraphs: Important for torsades de pointes and specific deficiency/toxicologic contexts.

lessons.title: Medication Concentration, Dilution & Dose Safety
lessons.summary: most catastrophic medication errors are system errors: wrong concentration, decimal, route or unit.

sections.title: 1) Unit discipline
paragraphs: Write mg, mcg, mL and mg/mL explicitly. Convert only one step at a time and avoid mental shortcuts when stress is high.

sections.title: 2) Dose-to-volume
paragraphs: Volume (mL) = required dose (mg) ÷ concentration (mg/mL). For weight-based drugs: required dose = dose/kg × weight.

sections.title: 3) Independent double-check
paragraphs: For high-alert drugs, verbally confirm patient/weight, indication, drug, concentration, calculated dose, volume, route and max dose with a second clinician when possible.

sections.title: 4) Decimal safety
paragraphs: Use leading zero (0.1), never trailing zero (1.0), and be alert to mg↔mcg thousand-fold errors.
